Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call hosted by Concept Investor Relations to discuss the 
company's financial and operational performance for the quarter and half year ended 
September 2026.  
Before we begin, let me mention a short cautionary statement. Some of the statements made 
in today's earnings call may be forward looking in nature. Such forward-looking statements are 
subject to risks and uncertainties which could cause actual results to differ from those 
anticipated.  
Such statements are made on management's beliefs as well as assumptions made by the 
information currently available to the management. Audiences are cautioned not to place any 
undue reliance on these forward-looking statements in making any investment decisions. The 
purpose of today's earnings call is purely to educate and bring awareness about the company's 
fundamental business and financial quarter under review.  
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing “*” and then “0” 
on your touchtone phone. 
Let me introduce you to the management, Mr. Jurgen Bailom – Executive Director and CEO, 
Mr. Nishikant Upadhyay – Chief Financial Officer. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Jurgen Bailom. Thank you and over to you, sir. 
Jurgen Bailom: 
Thank you, Sagar. Very good evening, everyone and thank you for joining us today for 
Waterways Leisure Tourism Limited Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Call. 
Joining me today is Mr. Nishikant Upadhyay – our Chief Financial Officer and our Investor 
Relations Partners, Concept Public Relations.  
 
Let me start with a little perspective on where we are as business today: 

 
Page 2 of 17 
We started Waterways Leisure Tourism in November 2020 and we set sail with Cordelia Cruises 
in September 2021. Over the last few years, we have built Cordelia into a strong cruise brand 
in India. From the very beginning, our goal was simply to create the premium cruise experience 
built around the Indian traveler and what they value most. For us a cruise is not just about the 
destination. 
It's about the complete holiday from food and entertainment, accommodation, family 
experiences, wellness and our guest experience both on board and ashore. Very pleased to say 
a key development as we enter the second half of FY27 is the delivery of Cordelia Sky, which 
has arrived in Mumbai today this morning at 8:00 A.M. at the beautiful International Cruise 
Terminal in Mumbai on schedule and will commence sailing from 23rd of October.  
The early delivery reflects a strong execution and operational efficiency while giving us 
additional time to complete preparation and ensure a smooth start to operations. With a 
capacity of 2,400 guests across 1,002 staterooms, Sky will increase our overall capacity by 
approximately 126%.  
More importantly, it gives us significantly greater flexibility to operate a wider range of 
domestic and international itineraries. Revenue from Sky will start contributing from second 
half of this financial year with the larger benefits building progressively as utilization ramps up. 
 
We are encouraged by the initial booking grants and we believe the additional capacity will 
allow us to serve a much broader range of customer occasions and travel preferences. For us, 
Sky is more than an addition to the fleet. It is an important step in expanding the number of 
occasions on which customers can choose Cordelia, whether for family holiday, weekend 
getaways, celebrations, a destination wedding or an international vacation. 
 
Coming up to our performance: 
Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter for us, with performance improving both year-on-year and 
sequentially. We have outperformed Q1 and delivered improvement despite a challenging 
external environment, including geopolitical uncertainty and broader macroeconomic 
headwinds. For us, this is an important message. 
 
While external conditions can influence travel patterns and consumer sentiments, our focus 
remains on what we can control demand generation, pricing, inventory management, 
customer experience and cost discipline. We have also seen additional revenue streams 
contributing to the business, reflecting the increasing breadth of our offering and opportunities 
we have to enhance revenue per guest.  
At the same time, cost management remains an important priority. We are taking an 
aggressive, but disciplined approach to sales and inventory management, balancing demand 

 
Page 3 of 17 
stimulation with pricing and capacity optimization. The objective is clear to drive higher 
utilization and revenue while protecting the quality of our earnings.  
Looking at the larger opportunities: 
We remain very positive of the long-term potential of cruising in India. India recorded 
approximately 4.8 lakh cruise passenger movements in CY 2025, while domestic passengers 
accounting for nearly 89%. The Indian overnight ocean and coastal cruise industry was valued 
at approximately ₹8,301 millionsin FY25 compared to ₹5,764 millions in FY20 and is expected 
to grow at around 20% to 25% CAGR between FY26 and FY31.  
Yet, cruise penetration in India remains very low relative to the overall travel and tourism 
opportunities. As consumers increasingly look for differentiated, experience-led holidays, we 
believe cruising is well-positioned to benefit from the structural shift by bringing 
accommodation, dining, entertainment and destinations together in one experience.  
India's extensive coastline is a significant structural advantage for the industry. In addition, 
wherever applicable, passport-free and visa-free cruise itineraries can reduce the friction 
associated with conventional international travel, further supporting cruising as an attractive 
and accessible holiday choice for Indian consumers.  
We therefore see a long runway for the category and believe our increasing scale, broad 
itinerary network and differentiated customer proposition, position us well to participate in 
this growth. With this broader travel opportunity, we are also seeing an encouraging 
opportunity in the weddings and celebration segment.  
Industry data indicates that FY28 could see approximately 95 wedding dates compared with a 
typical Calender of around 65 to 70, representing an increase of nearly 40%. With our cruise 
proposition and the additional capacity coming through Cordelia Sky, we believe we are well-
positioned to participate in this growing demand and further develop weddings and 
celebration as an attractive revenue stream across accommodation, dining, entertainment and 
other onboard services.  
As we continue to expand our fleet, we remain focused on building a larger and more scalable 
cruise platform. Alongside that delivery of our previously announced next vessel SUN remains 
on schedule. We are pleased to inform you that we are further exploring fleet expansion 
opportunities beyond SUN.  
We are at an initial discussion stage currently. While it's too early to provide specific details at 
this point, our direction remains clear. Progressively build capacity in line with the growth of 
the Indian cruise market. Our strong strategy is not simply about adding capacity. It's about 

 
Page 4 of 17 
deploying vessels across the right mix of itineraries, optimizing utilization and pricing and 
assuring that additional capacity translates into sustainable revenue, profitability growth. 
 
As we scale, our focus will remain on maintaining the quality of customer experience, while 
ensuring that growth is supported by operational and financial discipline. Along capacity 
expansion, we are also strengthening our relationship with our customers. As part of this, we 
are rolling out our loyalty program called the Chairman's Club. 
 
We believe a structured loyalty program can help us deepen engagement with our existing 
customer base, encourage repeat travel and create more opportunities to engage with 
customers beyond a single voyage. This is particularly relevant as we build a business where 
the same customer can travel with us on different occasions and across different destinations. 
Ultimately, our objective is to give customers more reasons to choose Cordelia and over time 
build stronger repeat engagement and customer values.  
With that, I will hand over to Nishikant to take you through the financial performance for the 
quarter and the first half. 
Nishikant Upadhyay: 
Thank you, Jurgen. Good evening, everyone. 
Let me take you through our financial performance for the quarter ended September 30, 
2026: 
For Quarter 2 Financial Year ‘27, revenue from operations stood at Rs. 1,329 million registering 
a year-on-year growth of 31% compared to Financial Year ‘26, value being Rs. 1,015 million in 
Quarter 2. 
 
EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 777 million with an EBITDA margin of 58.45%, while profit 
after tax stood at Rs. 585 million, translating into a PAT margin of 44.02% for the current 
quarter. For the half year Financial Year ‘27, revenue from operations stood at Rs. 3,230 billion, 
representing a year-on-year growth of 16%. EBITDA stood at Rs.1,242 million with an EBITDA 
margin of 38.45%. 
While PAT stood at Rs. 813 million with a PAT margin of 25.16%. During the quarter, the 
company has received USD 5.2 million in compensation from Norwegian Sky Limited for the 
early handover of the vessel Sky on September 10, 2026, ahead of its original delivery date of 
30th September 2026.  
This amount has been derived considering 21 days early delivery calculated basis on the 100% 
load factor and has been compensated by NCL as Jurgen, while introductory speech has rightly 
pointed out that, yes, we have taken the delivery and the vessel has truly arrived at Mumbai in 
the morning.

basis to 75.53% in Quarter 2 for the Financial Year ‘27. For the half year Financial Year ‘27, the

previous last year.  
 
Now gentlemen coming to the average ticket price for Quarter 2 Financial Year ‘27 stood at Rs. 
10,300 as compared to Rs. 9,529, while the half year Financial Year ‘27, average ticket price 
increased to Rs. 11,082 from Rs. 10,468 in half yearly, Financial Year ‘26. Average revenue per 
passenger stood at Rs. 13,645 in Quarter 2, financial year 27, compared with Rs. 10,349 in 
Quarter 2, Financial Year ‘26.  
 
For half yearly Financial Year ‘27, average revenue per passenger increased to Rs. 12,930 
against Rs. 11,424 for the corresponding period last year. These are all encouraging numbers. 
Fuel cost, which is a challenge. So, fuel cost per available passenger cruise day, APCD has 
increased to Rs. 2,471 in Quarter 2, financial year 2027, vis-a-vis which was Rs.1,434 in Quarter 
2 or financial year 2026.  
 
Half yearly Financial Year ‘27 fuel cost per APCD stood at Rs. 2,481 as compared to Rs. 1,472 in 
the corresponding period last year. Available passenger cruise days is basically how many 
cabins you have multiplied by number of two people into the number of days when you are 
sailing.  
So, if you talk about the collective number, the fuel impact for the half year  as compared to 
previous year and current year is almost to the extent of Rs. 28 odd crores. Had it would not 
have been there, the profits would have been more by Rs. 28 odd crores. Company has 
maintained a healthy debt-to-equity ratio of 0.57%, reflecting a balanced capital structure 
during the period.  
As Jurgen rightly mentioned, that yes, we are in the process of looking for further more vessels. 
And in line with this, we have advanced Rs.4,290 million towards the acquisition of new vessels. 
It is an advance which has been given and it is an interest-bearing advance. We continue to 
maintain a disciplined approach towards cost, while actively managing pricing and inventory to 
optimize revenue realization.  
With Cordelia Sky now delivered ahead of schedule, we will progressively evaluate its 
contribution to capacity, revenue, profitability as we commence operations. Overall, we 
remain focused on balancing growth, investment with financial discipline and ensuring that 
capacity expansion translates into sustainable improvement in earnings.  
While moving it back to Jurgen, I just need to mention that if we talk about increase in fuel cost 
of around Rs. 28 odd crores, as Jurgen has rightly mentioned that yes, we have been managing 
the cost effectively. So, there has been cost-shedding in various areas which has been

instrumental into absorbing the increase in the fuel price. With this, I will hand the call back to 
Jurgen.

Well, thank you very much, Nishikant and before we close, I would like to leave you with a few 
key takeaways. First Q2 and H1 FY27 was a stronger quarter for us with performance improving 
both sequentially and year-on-year despite challenging external environments. Second, the 
delivery of Cordelia Sky today, one month ahead of schedule marks an important step up in 
our capacity, in our ability to offer a wider range of itineraries and experiences.  
 
Third, we are strengthening the customer relations through initiatives such as our new loyalty

revenue optimization and cost management as we build the next phase of Waterways Leisure
